title: Deuteronomy: love the LORD with all your heart

lines: Deuteronomy is almost all speech. Moses is at the end of his life, on the plains of Moab, preaching to the children of the generation that left Egypt.
He tells the story again, gives the law again, and pleads with them to hold on to God when he's gone.

scripture.text: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel

lines: It has three addresses and a farewell. Moses looks back on the road. At the center he repeats the Ten Commandments and sets out the laws for the land. He renews the covenant. And he blesses the tribes.
One small word holds it all together. Today.

scripture.text: with all of us who are alive here today.

lines: At the center stand two verses called the Shema. One God, loved with heart, soul, and strength.
And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart.
Love here is a settled loyalty, shown in listening and obeying, and the words are meant to fill ordinary life. Jews have said them morning and evening for more than two thousand years.

scripture.text: And you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart

lines: God chose Israel not for its size or its goodness, but because he loved them.
Being chosen is a task. It's never a license to look down on anyone, and God loves the foreigner. So the great duty of the book is to remember.

scripture.text: But because the LORD loved you

chapters.kicker: Watch for: whose side the laws take
lines: The laws take the side of the powerless: the widow, the orphan, the foreigner, the debtor, the worker.

scripture.text: You are to pay his wages each day before sunset

lines: The command about the peoples of Canaan is the hardest page, and Christians read it in more than one way. On every reading, it was tied to one land and one time.
No one may use these chapters to justify violence against any person or people.
The blessings and curses of chapter twenty-eight speak to a nation about a land. They're never God's verdict on one person's illness or loss.
Then comes the promise that God will change the heart itself, and the plea to choose life.
I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing.
And Moses sees the land he will not enter.

scripture.text: I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing.

lines: Start with chapters six and thirty. Then the key chapters: one, four, eight, twelve, eighteen, and thirty-four. Read it as preaching, out loud.
And keep the order straight. God's love comes first, and obedience answers it.
titleCard: God's love comes first. Obedience answers it.
